blocks.text:
**Call PICU / transplant center now:** encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, renal failure, shock, or INR not corrected by IV vitamin K: ≥ 1.5 with encephalopathy or ≥ 2.0 without.
**Newborn, ill, with hepatitis:** think herpes simplex virus (HSV) — start IV acyclovir now.
**Possible acetaminophen ingestion with a raised ALT:** start IV N-acetylcysteine (NAC) now and send a level. ALT > 15 × upper limit of normal (ULN) with no clear cause: send a level.
**INR > 1.5:** give IV vitamin K, recheck INR, call hepatology today.
**Same-day hepatology:** jaundice, pale stools or dark urine; bleeding; ALT > 10 × ULN; liver mass; large liver or spleen, or low platelets.

groups.label: Tier 1 — persistent rise
items: ALT, AST, GGT, ALP; total and direct bilirubin
INR, albumin, CBC with platelets, glucose
Tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA) + total IgA (only if eating gluten)
HBsAg, anti-HCV (infant: HCV RNA if the mother is HCV-positive)
EBV serology (VCA); CMV (infant: PCR); HAV IgM if acute
IgG, ANA, smooth muscle antibody (SMA), anti-liver-kidney microsomal type 1 (anti-LKM1)

groups.label: Focused panel — teen with obesity or metabolic risk, ALT < 2 × ULN
items: ALT, AST, GGT, ALP; total and direct bilirubin
Acetaminophen — including repeated supratherapeutic dosing and self-harm: level now
Wilson disease — usually from age 3, rarely younger; treatable. Low ALP or Coombs-negative hemolysis in a sick child: think acute Wilson
Autoimmune hepatitis — modest ALT with high IgG; autoantibodies can be negative
Muscular dystrophy — boy with ALT and AST up: CK before any liver workup
Celiac disease — tTG-IgA with total IgA
Chronic HBV or HCV — ALT can be normal
A1AT deficiency — the level alone can be falsely normal in an acute-phase response
Infants: congenital infection (CMV, HSV), metabolic disease, gestational alloimmune liver disease (GALD)

blocks.text:
ALT sits in the hepatocyte cytosol (half-life about 47 h). AST is also in muscle, heart and red cells (half-life about 17 h), so it falls first. AST above ALT points to muscle, hemolysis, macro-AST or advanced disease (Dufour 2000).

Lab ULNs run too high. The median ALT ULN at US children's hospitals was 53 U/L (range 30–90), while the 95th centile in healthy teens was 25.8 U/L in boys and 22.1 U/L in girls. Hospital cut-offs found 32–48% of children with NAFLD (now MASLD), HBV or HCV; health-based cut-offs found 72–82% (SAFETY 2010).

In Naples, 425 children had isolated raised transaminases: 61% normalized within 6 months. Of 166 with a persistent rise, one in three had a genetic disease — Wilson 18, muscular dystrophy 14, A1AT 4, Alagille 4, hereditary fructose intolerance 4, glycogen storage disease IX 3 (Iorio 2005). Repeat first: the second abnormal result is where treatable diseases hide.

In 120 obese, symptom-free children with ALT ≥ 40 U/L, extensive testing added little and produced false positives (Rudolph 2015). Pre-test probability decides the panel.

items.text: From age 11, read ALT against 26 U/L (boys) or 22 U/L (girls), whatever the lab prints. AASLD applies these from age 10.
Repeat, but not twice — the second abnormal result starts the workup.
Raised ALT and AST in a boy: check CK before any liver test or biopsy. Duchenne diagnosis was delayed by a liver workup in 6 boys (McMillan 2011).
In adults, weightlifting raised ALT and AST for at least 7 days (Pettersson 2008). Ask about exercise; repeat after ≥ 7 days, ideally 2 weeks, of rest.
Falling ALT with rising INR and bilirubin = loss of liver mass, not recovery.

In jaundice, a low ALP is a red flag. ALP:bilirubin < 4 and AST:ALT > 2.2 each had 94% sensitivity for acute Wilson failure in a mixed adult–pediatric cohort (Korman 2008). In 40 children with Wilson liver failure, sensitivity fell to 32.5% (ALP:bilirubin < 4) and 77.5% (AST:ALT ≥ 1.85) (Yasmin 2022). A negative ratio does not exclude Wilson.
A normal ALT in a child with obesity is not a normal liver if the lab ULN is 40 U/L or more.
Isolated AST with normal ALT and CK → macro-AST.

positions.seghnp_2022_htra: > 40 U/L boys, > 35 U/L girls over 18 months; > 60 / > 55 under 18 months; 26 / 22 for teen screening
positions.aasld_2025_masld_peds: > 26 U/L boys, > 22 U/L girls from age 10; no validated cut-off under 10
positions.espghan_2026_masld: ALT ≥ 30 U/L as the MASLD screening test (over 10 y with obesity, or any age with risk factors)

rows.note: The app reads ALT against 26/22 from age 11 and against the lab range below that. Lesson 01-01 reads AASLD as using 30 U/L for younger children — a population-study convention, not a validated limit.

rows.topic: First response to a raised ALT

positions.seghnp_2022_htra: Confirm in 2–4 weeks (up to 8 if a transient cause is likely)
positions.aasld_2025_masld_peds: Repeat within 3 months; 24–48 h if acute hepatitis is suspected
positions.espghan_2026_masld: MASLD screen: ALT 30–80, repeat in 2–6 months; ≥ 80, clinical assessment and investigations

rows.note: The app repeats in 2–4 weeks if the child is well and ALT is under 5 × ULN, and starts tier 1 at once above that. ESPGHAN's rule (repeat only if there is no concern for acute liver disease; 80 U/L) applies to MASLD screening in obese children (the app uses it in the teen branch); its figure says "over 80", its text "≥ 80".
The app adds CK to the first repeat in every child: a missed muscular dystrophy costs a liver biopsy (McMillan 2011).

positions.espghan_2026_masld: Only if AIH is suspected (first-line: immunoglobulins, ANA, SMA)

rows.note: The app puts autoantibodies and IgG in tier 1: type 2 AIH (anti-LKM1) affects young children.

positions.kwo_2017_acg_lft: Ceruloplasmin if the rise persists, under 55 y

rows.note: All screen for Wilson disease; they differ on when. The app tests ceruloplasmin in tier 1 from age 3 — Wilson is treatable and fatal if missed.

positions.seghnp_2022_htra: Level in tier 2, phenotype in tier 3

rows.note: The app sends level + phenotype together in tier 1: the level alone can be falsely normal.

positions.bsg_2018_lft: May not be indicated in children

rows.note: Hereditary hemochromatosis rarely presents in childhood; the app does not order iron studies routinely.
Pediatric documents test thyroid function in every child; ACG only if the history suggests it.

positions.seghnp_2022_htra: Consider at 12–18 months if still undiagnosed
positions.espghan_2026_masld: MASLD: reserve for diagnostic uncertainty, treatment decisions and risk staging

rows.note: Only SEGHNP gives a timeline for unexplained raised transaminases.
